name: feedback-as-data-audit
question: Does any code path let feedback-derived (public-internet) text reach the implementer's instruction/system layer instead of the single untrusted-data envelope (25b), or let an outbound payload bypass the egress sanitizer chokepoint and leak source/secrets (25c)? Probe A proves the prompt data-envelope has exactly one chokepoint (prompt::wrap_untrusted) + the DEC-84 preamble. Probe B proves every outbound POST routes through sanitizer::sanitize_outbound (reusing the canonical PII scrubber). Probe C (--full) runs the C24 adversarial corpus incl. the P5b (g)/(f) cases.

output.schema: PASS or FAIL <n> with probe-level offender detail. Exit 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL, 2 on environment failure. Probe A LIVE in Stage 0 (chokepoint present; full-assembly tightening activates when Worker A finalizes prompt::assemble). Probe B reports PENDING until the outbound modules (report/analyst) land. Probe C reports PENDING while the P5b corpus cases remain #[ignore].

consultation.typical_sessions_using: every-commit touching the runner prompt assembly, the egress sanitizer, or the C24 corpus

consumer_scope: feedbackmonk: Worker A (primary — a green oracle with Probe B+C ACTIVE is Worker A's Stage-1 exit gate) + every reviewer touching crates/feedbackmonk-runner/src/{prompt,sanitizer,implementer}.rs, the runner outbound paths (report/analyst), or the C24 corpus.
fallback: Probe A: read crates/feedbackmonk-runner/src/prompt.rs and confirm (1) `fn wrap_untrusted` exists + builds the `<untrusted-feedback-data>` envelope; (2) the DEC-84 preamble const is present; (3) the envelope literal appears in NO other runner source file (single chokepoint). Probe B: read crates/feedbackmonk-runner/src/sanitizer.rs and confirm `fn sanitize_outbound` exists + reuses feedbackmonk_tracing::scrub; then confirm every outbound POST module (report/analyst) routes its payload through it. Probe C: cargo test -p feedbackmonk-api --test feedback_injection_corpus.

provenance.authored_by: P5b Stage 0 (Task Zero scaffold) — finalized by Worker A as prompt.rs / sanitizer.rs land
provenance.rationale: Testability Gate Flags 1 & 2 (the highest plan-wide fidelity risk, Q2=5 on both the implementer/prompt-envelope and the outbound sanitizer): P5b is where public-internet feedback first reaches a code-writing agent. A happy-path 'the prompt looks right' unit test confirms ONE assembly; it cannot prove the ABSENCE of a prompt-injection bypass (feedback text reaching the instruction layer) nor an outbound path that skips the sanitizer (a source/secret leak). This oracle is detection-from-CODE (single-chokepoint static assertions + the C24 corpus), the anti-reward-hacking leg per Contract C27 — it cannot be satisfied by a self-reported flag. Scaffolded in Stage 0 (Probe A live; B/C co-evolve with Worker A); a green oracle is Worker A's exit gate. The exact analogue of approval-gate-enforcement for P5a, on the surface now live with code execution.
